nightly-bot: Nightly eval (2026-03-19 07:00 UTC) -- 14 fails, 9 regressions flagged. Failing suite: tool-calling/json-schema-checks. Report: https://ci.redwood/internal/nightly/1799991234
Samir: heads-up — one of the failing prompts is returning a tool output where the payload is an escaped JSON string instead of a native array/object. validator throws: > 'expected array, got string'
Samir: example from logs:
```
tool_response = {
  \"tool\": \"action_runner\",
  \"result\": \"[{'action': 'open', 'target': 'url', 'value': 'https://example.com'}]\"
}
```
Anya: ugh, looks like the result field is double-quoted but inside it's single-quoted Python repr. Which model/commit?
Samir: happens only on v2-quant-5b @ commit 0f3a1c9; non-quant variants are fine. repro attached in CI link above.
Kevin: short-term we should make the eval harness more forgiving: if schema expects array/object and we get a string, attempt reparsing with json.loads, then fallback to ast.literal_eval. Log both the original and the parsed value.
Maria: agreed we need a fallback, but also flag an infra bug. The wrapper that calls the external tool should return proper JSON. We shouldn't silently accept Python repr forever.
Samir: also saw some cases where the tool returned a JSON string that used single quotes and trailing commas, e.g.:
```
\"[{'action': 'open', 'target': 'url', 'value': 'https://x',}, ]\"
```
Samir: json.loads will fail on that. ast.literal_eval helps, but it's risky if the tool starts returning arbitrary objects.
Anya: any quick mitigation that doesn't mask errors? maybe add a strict flag in the harness: permissive_for_nightly=true, but only for 48 hrs while infra patch rolls out. And emit an eval-warning metric.
Kevin: plan: 1) add fallback parser in nightly eval harness (json.loads -> ast.literal_eval -> regex-fix -> fail). 2) increment a counter metric when fallback is used. 3) fail the nightly (keep as regression) but mark cause as \"parse_fallback_used\" so PMs see infra issue. I'll pick this up.
Samir: sketch of fallback function I tested locally:
```python
import json, ast, re

def safe_parse_tool_output(raw):
    # raw is expected to be a string or already-parsed obj
    if not isinstance(raw, str):
        return raw
    try:
        return json.loads(raw)
    except Exception:
        pass
    try:
        return ast.literal_eval(raw)
    except Exception:
        pass
    # last-ditch: convert single quotes to double and remove trailing commas
    s = re.sub(r\",\s*}\", '}', raw)
    s = re.sub(r\",\s*\]\", ']', s)
    s = s.replace("'", '\"')
    try:
        return json.loads(s)
    except Exception as e:
        raise ValueError(f\"unparseable tool output: {e}\")
```
Kevin: I'll add logging around each branch and a metric `eval_tool_parse_fallback_total`.
Maria: can you also add a boolean flag in the nightly UI so reviewers can filter failures caused by parse fallback? saves time when triaging regressions.
Kevin: yep. I'll send a PR against infra/eval-harness and include tests for: valid json string, python repr, single-quotes + trailing-commas.
Samir: created a ticket and linked it in the CI log: https://tickets.redwood/ISSUE-4821 — assigned to @kevin, label: infra-tool-wrapper, priority: P2 :thumbsup:
Anya: thanks. Also pinging infra channel to get the tool wrapper fixed (it probably started returning reprs after a recent upgrade to the runner). @Maria can you loop in infra?
Maria: on it. I'll open an incident if we see >5% of tool calls using fallback.
